name: Dusty peach
lede: Dusty peach is a pale tan with a warm pink cast, ColorHub's English name for the Japanese traditional color Torinoko-iro, "eggshell paper color."

sections.title: The color of eggshell paper
sections.body:
Torinoko-iro (鳥の子色) is named in the Wikipedia list of Japan's traditional colors for *torinoko-gami*, a smooth, cream-colored handmade paper whose name literally means "bird's child," or egg, paper [1]. The color describes the paper's pale, warm tone rather than an egg itself [1].

The nearest named colors on file are [[pale-flesh]] and [[flesh-red]], at 2.9 and 2.9 ΔE [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this color in 858 of 23,781 paintings, about 3.6 percent, as photographed [2]. The earliest match is a Chinese painting by Zhao Guangfu, *Barbarian Royalty Worshiping the Buddha*, dated to about 900, though the matching area is small, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2]. The rate peaks in a sample of 169 paintings from the 1710s, about two and a half times the archive's overall rate for that decade [2]. Among sampled painters, Xugu's sixteen paintings contain it eleven times, by far the highest rate recorded, well ahead of Thomas Cole and Kano Tan'yū [2]. It is also disproportionately common in paintings from India, Japan, Korea, Iran and China [2]. These are computed color matches to photographed, varnished paintings, not pigment identifications [2].

notes.cite: ColorHub archive (23,781 paintings), computed match, as photographed

questions.q: What does Torinoko-iro name this color after?
Which painter's sampled works show the highest rate of this color?

openers: Named for paper, not fruit, and most at home in paintings from East and South Asia.
